2607.25995.title: Does Runtime Topology Context Improve LLM-Generated Kubernetes Security Patches?
2607.25995.paper_summary: Kubernetes is central to the cloud-native ecosystem, orchestrating containerised workloads. Recent work suggests that large language models (LLMs) can automate cluster security remediation, generating configuration patches from Kubernetes Security Posture Management (KSPM) findings without human authoring. Such systems, however, prompt the model with each finding in isolation from the live service call graph, assuming general hardening knowledge suffices. This assumption breaks down whenever a patch must preserve a runtime service dependency invisible to the model: an otherwise compliant fix then carries a destructive functional blast radius, crashing downstream callers or silently severing call edges across the cluster. Whether live cluster context improves patch correctness has not been measured under controlled conditions across multiple dependency classes. We introduce KuTIE (Kubernetes Topology Intelligence Engine), which builds a live cluster context from Istio call edges, Trivy KSPM findings, and the service-account bindings a workload reads, and conditions LLM patch generation on it. It is evaluated on VulnCare, a purpose-built 36-deployment, four-namespace healthcare cluster with 31 injectable findings across seven dependency classes, each labelled by topology dependence against cluster ground truth. Across 248 trials, topology context raises topology-dependent patch correctness from 11.1% to 78.0% ($Δ= 0.669$), a gap that holds for every model and for six of seven classes, from credential and network-policy ($Δ= 0.95$) to role-based access control ($Δ= 0.31$); a topology-independent control exhibits no such effect ($Δ= 0.0$), isolating the result from generic prompt enrichment. Supplying the live service-call graph and the service-account bindings it exposes thus improves remediation of topology-dependent findings well beyond scanner-only context.
2607.25995.paper_summary_zh: Kubernetes 是雲原生生態系統的核心，負責協調容器化工作負載。最近的研究表明，大型語言模型 (LLMs) 可以自動化叢集安全修復，根據 Kubernetes 安全姿態管理 (KSPM) 的發現生成配置修補，而無需人工編寫。然而，這些系統在每次發現時都會向模型提出問題，與實時服務調用圖隔離，假設一般的加固知識足夠。這一假設在修補必須保留模型無法看到的運行時服務依賴時會失效：一個原本合規的修復可能會帶來破壞性的功能影響，導致下游調用者崩潰或靜默中斷叢集中的調用邊緣。在受控條件下，是否實時叢集上下文能改善修補的正確性尚未被測量，且跨越多個依賴類別。我們介紹了 KuTIE（Kubernetes 拓撲智能引擎），它從 Istio 調用邊緣、Trivy KSPM 發現以及工作負載讀取的服務帳戶綁定構建實時叢集上下文，並以此為條件生成 LLM 修補。它在 VulnCare 上進行評估，這是一個專門構建的 36 部署、四個命名空間的醫療叢集，擁有 31 個可注入的發現，跨越七個依賴類別，每個類別均標記為相對於叢集真實情況的拓撲依賴。在 248 次試驗中，拓撲上下文將依賴於拓撲的修補正確性從 11.1% 提高到 78.0% ($Δ= 0.669$)，這一差距在每個模型和七個類別中的六個類別中均存在，從憑證和網絡策略 ($Δ= 0.95$) 到基於角色的訪問控制 ($Δ= 0.31$)；而一個獨立於拓撲的對照則未顯示出這種效果 ($Δ= 0.0$)，將結果與通用提示增強隔離開來。因此，提供實時服務調用圖及其暴露的服務帳戶綁定，顯著改善了對依賴於拓撲的發現的修復，遠超過僅依賴掃描器的上下文。
2607.25995.author: Farooq Shaikh et.al.
